title: Improving interface-mediated carrier transport for efficient perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 tandem solar cells - Nature Energy
gist: A Wuhan University-led team reports monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem cells at 31.09% power conversion efficiency (certified 30.57%) on 0.0539 cm2 devices and 29.44% (certified 28.85%) at ~1 cm2, using a nanoparticle NiOX intermediate recombination layer plus bimolecular co-passivation at the perovskite/C60 interface to conformally cover textured CIGS. Only the abstract, figure titles, references and funding block are outside the paywall, but they show the perovskite/CIGS class crossing 30% for the first time (prior cited certified record: 27.35%) with stability retention of ~90-94% across storage, operation and 70 °C heat tests.

insights.claim: Monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 tandem cells reached 31.09% power conversion efficiency with a certified 30.57% and 30.32% steady-state on a 0.0539 cm2 device.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: CIGS-based tandems now sit in the same efficiency band as perovskite/silicon tandems, reopening thin-film PV as a credible high-efficiency route rather than a legacy niche.
insights.quote: Champion monolithic tandem cells achieve power conversion efficiencies of 31.09% (certified 30.57%, steady-state 30.32%) for small-area devices (0.0539 cm2)

insights.claim: The cited prior benchmark for a certified monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandem was 27.35%, so this result represents a step of roughly three percentage points in certified efficiency for the architecture.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A ~3pp certified jump in one publication cycle signals the technology is still on a steep part of its learning curve, which pressures incumbent single-junction silicon roadmaps.
insights.quote: Inhibiting defect passivation failure in perovskite for perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 monolithic tandem solar cells with certified efficiency 27.35%.

insights.claim: A 2022 review of the same architecture framed the goal as moving 'from certified 24.2% toward 30% and beyond', a target this work now reports as achieved four years later.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Gives a concrete cadence for thin-film tandem progress (~6pp in four years) that can be extrapolated when underwriting PV technology-risk assumptions.
insights.quote: Perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells: from certified 24.2% toward 30% and beyond.

insights.claim: Scaling the device area from 0.0539 cm2 to 1.0298 cm2 costs roughly 1.7 percentage points of certified efficiency, dropping from 30.57% to 28.85%.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: The lab-to-module gap remains the binding commercial constraint; headline champion-cell numbers overstate what a manufacturable module would deliver by at least this margin, and further at full module size.

insights.claim: Even the 'large-area' device in this study is only ~1 cm2, meaning no data is presented at module scale for the reported architecture.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Treat any near-term commercialization claim built on this result skeptically; the missing scale-up evidence is where capital risk concentrates.

themes.theme: Stability data and the durability gap

insights.claim: The optimized tandem devices retained ~94% of initial efficiency after >3,500 h of storage, ~91% after >750 h of continuous operation, and ~90% after 960 h of heating at 70 °C.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: 750-960 hours is roughly one to two months of stress testing against the 25-year warranties PV buyers demand; the durability evidence base is still orders of magnitude short of bankability.
insights.quote: The optimized devices retain ~94% of their initial efficiency after >3,500 h of storage, ~91% after >750 h of continuous operation, and ~90% after 960 h of heating at 70 °C

insights.claim: Efficiency and stability were improved simultaneously rather than traded off, which contradicts the usual perovskite pattern where passivation gains for efficiency degrade operational lifetime.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: If the efficiency-stability tradeoff is genuinely breakable at the interface level, the main technical objection to perovskite tandem commercialization weakens.
insights.quote: demonstrating simultaneously enhanced efficiency and stability

insights.claim: Separate cited work achieved over 1,000 h of operational stability in perovskite/CIGS tandems specifically through interconnection stress relief, indicating that the tandem interconnect - not just the perovskite absorber - is a distinct degradation pathway.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Mechanical/interconnect engineering, not only chemistry, is a separate lever and a separate supplier opportunity in tandem PV.
insights.quote: Perovskite/CIGS tandem solar cells with over 1000 h operational stability through interconnection stress relief

insights.claim: The stated limiting factor for monolithic perovskite/CIGS tandems is interfacial optical and electronic loss, not bulk absorber quality.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Value in the tandem stack is migrating to thin interfacial layers and passivation chemistries - specialty materials suppliers, not absorber makers, capture that margin.
insights.quote: are currently limited by interfacial optical and electronic losses
insights.locator: Abstract - Monolithic perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 tandem solar cells

insights.claim: The specific technical mechanism is a dual-interface strategy pairing a nanoparticle-assisted NiOX intermediate recombination layer with bimolecular co-passivation at the perovskite/C60 interface.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: NiOX nanoparticle inks and fullerene-interface passivator molecules become the identifiable consumable inputs to watch as tandem lines scale.
insights.quote: a dual-interface carrier transport engineering strategy that combines a nanoparticle-assisted NiOX intermediate recombination layer with bimolecular co-passivation at the perovskite/C60 interface

insights.claim: Conformal coverage of textured CIGS surfaces is called out as an enabling requirement, meaning the rough bottom-cell morphology of CIGS is the core process difficulty distinguishing this architecture from perovskite/silicon.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Deposition-equipment vendors capable of conformal coating on rough substrates (ALD, sputtering, solution routes) are the picks-and-shovels exposure to CIGS tandems.
insights.quote: enabling conformal coverage on textured Cu(In,Ga)Se2 surfaces, suppressed defects, optimized band alignment and enhanced carrier extraction across both interfaces

insights.claim: Cited prior work reached >26% efficiency in two-terminal perovskite/CIGS tandems using conformal coatings on commercial bottom cells, showing the architecture can be built on already-manufactured CIGS rather than bespoke research substrates.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Existing CIGS production lines could be retrofit targets rather than stranded assets - relevant to any surviving thin-film manufacturer's asset value.
insights.quote: Two-terminal perovskite/Cu(In,Ga)Se2 tandems with conformal coatings based on commercial bottom cells with >26% efficiency

themes.theme: Chinese state funding of tandem PV

insights.claim: The work is funded through China's National Key Research and Development Program (grant 2024YFB4205300), Jiangsu province's 'Dual Carbon' innovation fund, and multiple national and provincial science foundations, with all listed institutions in China.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
entities: National Key Research and Development Program of China
insights.so_what: Next-generation PV efficiency leadership is being produced inside a Chinese state funding stack, implying the industrialization path and supply chain for tandem PV will likely be Chinese first.
insights.quote: the National Key Research and Development Program of China (grant no. 2024YFB4205300)

insights.claim: Efficiency certification itself required dedicated funding secured by named co-authors, indicating third-party certification is a nontrivial cost gate in the PV record-chasing process.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Certified-vs-claimed efficiency gaps in the literature partly reflect who can afford certification, a useful filter when reading PV records.
insights.quote: X.W. and G.C. contributed to efficiency certification funding

insights.claim: The reference list shows three tandem families competing in parallel - perovskite/silicon, all-perovskite, and perovskite/CIGS - with the CIGS route uniquely positioned for flexible and lightweight formats including steel-substrate and sub-26.5% flexible devices.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: CIGS tandems may win on form factor (flexible, lightweight, BIPV, vehicle-integrated) rather than on cost per watt against silicon - a different addressable market than utility-scale.

insights.claim: The article is published behind a paywall with only the abstract, figure captions, references and author metadata publicly accessible, so the mechanistic evidence and full device statistics cannot be independently assessed from the open text.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Any downstream claim sourced only to this page rests on the abstract's self-reported numbers; certification bodies and the next Solar Cell Efficiency Tables are the verification to wait for.
